belief: Church tradition carries the same authority as Scripture.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that church tradition carries the same authority as Scripture, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Growing up where long-standing customs were treated as unquestionable. Hearing “we’ve always done it this way” as if it were God’s command. Strong family or cultural ties to certain church practices. Not knowing where specific traditions came from. Christian traditions differ on how tradition and Scripture relate; this card focuses on the danger of letting any human tradition override God’s Word.
teaches: Many church traditions are good and helpful: they can preserve wisdom, guard truth, and help us worship. But Jesus rebuked religious leaders for setting aside God’s commands to keep human traditions, and for nullifying God’s Word by their traditions. Scripture is God-breathed and stands forever. Traditions are valuable when they serve Scripture and must be corrected when they conflict with it.
self_statements: If my church has always done it, God must require it.
Our customs are just as holy as the Bible.
I’ll be in trouble with God if I don’t follow every tradition.
Tradition is the same as truth.
errors: Treating human practices as if God commanded them.
Believing you must either keep every tradition or reject them all.
Assuming something is true because it is old.
Avoiding examination because change feels threatening.
questions: What did Jesus say about traditions that set aside God’s commands?
Where did this tradition come from? Is it in Scripture?
Does this tradition help me follow God’s Word or replace it?
Can I value tradition and still put Scripture first?
What stands forever: God’s Word or human customs?
Am I afraid of God, or afraid of what people will think?
Which traditions in my life truly draw me closer to God?
truth: Church traditions can be good gifts, but they do not carry the same authority as Scripture. God’s Word is God-breathed and stands forever. I can honor traditions that help me follow Christ, and I can set aside any tradition that contradicts or replaces His Word.
hw_questions: What did Jesus say about traditions that replace God’s commands?
Where did this tradition come from?
Does it help me follow God’s Word or replace it?
Can I value tradition and still put Scripture first?
Am I afraid of God or of people?
hw_truths: The word of our God stands forever.
Traditions are good when they serve Scripture.
I can honor helpful traditions without making them equal to the Bible.
I follow Christ, not just customs.
log: List one tradition I practice, where it came from, and whether it helps me follow Scripture.
name_example: If Sarah continues in My word, she is truly My disciple. Then she will know the truth, and the truth will set her free.
actions: Choose one church tradition you follow
and research where it came from and what Scripture says about it.
and write in your own words what Jesus was correcting.
Talk with your pastor or priest
about how your church understands tradition and Scripture.
Name one tradition that truly helps you draw near to God,
tracker: One practice I checked against Scripture
prayer: Father, thank You for Your Word, which stands forever. Help me reject the lie that church tradition carries the same authority as Scripture. Thank You for traditions that help me worship and follow You. Give me wisdom to keep what is good and courage to put Your Word first. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: Christ’s sacrifice answers guilt and the effort to pay for one’s own sins.
Receive God’s Word with humility and allow truth to reshape thought and action.
Jesus is present in suffering and is greater than the circumstances we face.
